name: Jordan
label: Podcast-UI critic, music loyalist
who: I listen to podcasts in the car on my way to work and rely on the New Episodes feed to catch up on the shows I follow. I have used both free and paid Spotify, and I care most about a clean podcast feed and keeping my playlists in one app.
value_for_money: They describe both free and paid use. One paid user says they pay a high price for podcast video that they cannot switch on in the car ([37]), and another cancelled a family plan over parental controls ([23]). Someone compares Spotify to YouTube Music and calls YouTube Music cheaper ([8]). No specific Spotify price is given, so they weigh cost against app quality.
loyalty: They stay for their playlists, the music library, the Spotify UI they like, and Wrapped, plus the convenience of having everything in one app ([20], [24], [27]). What would make them leave is podcast features that feel broken, such as lost episode folders or reversed episode order. Some have already left for Apple Podcasts, Apple Music, Pocket Casts or YouTube Music ([16], [23], [25], [27]).
pain_points: Removal of the New Episodes folder and no way to clear finished episodes
Unwanted podcasts stuck on the homepage or autoplaying
Podcasts showing up empty or missing from Wrapped and follow lists
likes: The Spotify UI, which they describe as attractive
Favorite podcasts available in the app
reasons_to_stay: They value their playlists and music library and say they love the UI ([20]). They also like Wrapped ([24]) and would rather keep podcasts in the same app as their music than split them across services ([27]), so they keep using Spotify while complaining about the podcast experience.
tone: Detailed and frustrated, often long and specific about interface changes, with some casual lowercase and sharp sarcasm.
